title: Function overload differentiation
recap: Overloads can differ by parameter number or parameter types. Renaming a parameter, changing only its default, or changing only the return type does not create a distinct overload.
The same operation can serve different domains while retaining domain-appropriate comparisons. For strings, compare text values rather than raw storage addresses.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement sameValue(int,int) and sameValue(std::string_view,std::string_view). Return exact equality for each pair. Text comparison is case-sensitive and compares contents, not addresses. Empty text equals empty text. Parameter names and return types are not what distinguish these overloads.
hints: Use the equality operator on the typed arguments.
A string_view comparison examines its characters.
Do not make the text overload case-insensitive.
